headline: 2,766 specimens, 2,667 isolates and 20,826 susceptibility results from 19 laboratories.

timeliness.note: The most recent specimen is over a month old. Submissions are behind.

rows.reason: Glycopeptides cannot cross the Gram-negative outer membrane. A susceptible result is not possible and indicates a testing or data-entry error.
Polymyxins act on the Gram-negative outer-membrane lipopolysaccharide, which Gram-positive organisms do not have.
Pseudomonas aeruginosa is intrinsically resistant to aminopenicillins.
Glycopeptides cannot cross the Gram-negative outer membrane. A susceptible result is not possible and indicates a testing or data-entry error.

suppression.summary: No cell was withheld. Every value shown rests on at least 1 records.

rows.consequence: Use can be reported as a volume only, and volumes cannot be compared between facilities or regions.
Consumption can be reported as a mass only, which reflects herd size as much as prescribing.

metrics.Numerator: Total defined daily doses dispensed in the group
metrics.Denominator: Total patient-days reported by the same facilities over the same periods
metrics.Conversion: Where DDD is not reported directly it is recovered as ddd_per_1000 x patient_days / 1000, so a record contributes only when it carries both
metrics.Calculation: sum(DDD) / sum(patient-days) x 1000. Pooled, not the mean of each record's rate: averaging rates weights a clinic reporting three prescriptions equally with a hospital reporting thirty thousand
metrics.Intended use: Comparing antimicrobial use between facilities, regions or periods on a common denominator
metrics.Not to be used for: Comparing against a facility that did not report patient-days, or inferring appropriateness -- volume is not quality

metrics.Denominator: None. This is a volume, not a rate
metrics.Conversion: None. Units are as submitted and may differ between facilities
metrics.Intended use: Describing procurement and workload within one facility or one unit of measure
metrics.Not to be used for: Comparing regions or facilities. A region with more hospitals dispenses more without using more per patient, and the units may not even be the same

metrics.Metric: Milligrams of active ingredient per kilogram of biomass
metrics.Denominator: Total biomass of the population at risk, in kilograms
metrics.Conversion: quantity_kg is taken to be active-ingredient mass and converted at 1,000,000 mg per kg. Where a submission reports product mass rather than active ingredient, the figure overstates use and the submission must be corrected at source
metrics.Calculation: sum(active ingredient mg) / sum(biomass kg). Pooled, not the mean of each record's ratio
metrics.Intended use: Comparing veterinary antimicrobial consumption between species, production systems or periods
metrics.Not to be used for: Comparing against human DDD figures, which use an entirely different denominator
